Participant guide

How do clinical studies work?

A clinical study is research involving people that helps answer questions about disease prevention, diagnosis or treatment.

From laboratory research to participation

Preclinical research

Before an intervention is studied in people, laboratory and preclinical evidence is reviewed to understand how it works and identify safety signals.

Protocol and review

Specialists define objectives, visits, procedures, safety measures and analysis. Independent ethics and regulatory review takes place before enrollment.

Voluntary participation

Participants receive clear information, provide informed consent and may ask questions or decide not to participate.

Study phases

Phase 1

Initial assessment of safety, tolerability and dosage.

Phase 2

Evaluation of preliminary effectiveness and continued safety.

Phase 3 and 4

Confirmation in larger populations and ongoing monitoring after authorization.
